steps.tx: First line treatment is a **benzodiazepine**: intravenous **lorazepam** 0.1 mg/kg, or intramuscular **midazolam** when there is no line. Underdosing the benzodiazepine is the common error. Prompt administration of full weight-based doses terminates seizure activity before GABA receptor internalization leads to pharmacoresistance.

steps.tx: **RAMPART** showed that **intramuscular midazolam** was at least as effective as intravenous lorazepam in the prehospital setting. Do not delay the first dose to place a drip. Rapid autoinjector or intramuscular injection achieves therapeutic brain levels faster by eliminating vascular access delays in seizing patients.

rows: Do not delay anticonvulsant to establish peripheral cannula

steps.tx: **ESETT** found that **levetiracetam**, **fosphenytoin**, and **valproate** were equivalent as the second line drug. One of them is given immediately after the benzodiazepine, at a full loading dose. Choosing any of the three established agents achieves approximately fifty percent seizure termination in established benzodiazepine-refractory status.

left.title: ESETT trial drug dosing
points: Fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg IV (maximum 1500 mg PE)

right.title: Clinical equivalence
points: Approximately 50% cessation rate across all three arms
Equivalent safety profiles regarding hypotension and intubation
Infuse full weight-adjusted loading dose over 10 minutes

steps.tx: **Refractory status epilepticus**, continuing after benzodiazepine and a second drug, is treated with a **midazolam** or **propofol** infusion and continuous EEG. **Ketamine** is an adjunct when those fail. General anaesthesia is titrated to achieve electrographic burst suppression, arresting ongoing excitotoxic neuronal necrosis.

Ketamine is an adjunct when those fail. General anaesthesia is titrated to achieve electrographic burst suppression, arresting ongoing excitotoxic neuronal necrosis.

rows: Watch for PRIS, hypertriglyceridaemia, and metabolic acidosis
Titrate to continuous electrographic burst suppression
1 to 2 mg/kg bolus then 1 to 5 mg/kg/h
Blocks upregulated NMDA receptors in prolonged status

steps.tx: **Super refractory status** is defined when seizures continue despite 24 hours of anaesthetic infusion. The search turns to **autoimmune encephalitis**, a missed metabolic cause, and a specialist anaesthetic plan. Consideration of NORSE and testing for anti-NMDAR antibodies warrants early immunotherapy with methylprednisolone, intravenous immunoglobulin, or plasma exchange.

left.title: Aetiological investigation
points: Screen for paraneoplastic and autoimmune antibodies
Perform lumbar puncture for viral PCR and oligoclonal bands
High-resolution brain MRI and toxicological screens

right.title: Therapeutic escalation
points: Intravenous immunoglobulin or therapeutic plasma exchange
Ketogenic diet and inhalational isoflurane anaesthesia

steps.tx: **Nonconvulsive status** is in the differential of unexplained coma after a convulsion. **EEG** makes the diagnosis. A normal CT does not exclude it. Electrographic seizure activity frequently persists after motor manifestations have ceased, maintaining continuous cerebral metabolic strain and secondary ischaemic neuronal death.

rows: Look for rhythmic epileptiform discharges or evolving patterns
Diagnoses nonconvulsive status without gross tonic-clonic jerks
Cannot exclude ongoing nonconvulsive electrographic status

steps.tx: **Glucose** is checked at once. **Hyponatraemia**, hypoxia, and a **toxic alcohol** are treated as causes, not as spectators, while the seizure drugs are given. Correcting acute metabolic derangements and reversing cerebral hypoperfusion is essential to terminate refractory seizures driven by systemic neurochemical disturbances.

left.title: Rapid metabolic screening
points: Electrolyte panel focusing on sodium and calcium
Arterial blood gas identifying severe anoxia or acidosis

right.title: Targeted corrective therapy
points: Hypertonic 3% saline bolus for acute hyponatraemic seizures
Specific antidotes for isoniazid or ethylene glycol

steps.tx: **Valproate** is avoided in known mitochondrial disease, pregnancy when an alternative exists, and significant **liver failure**. **Fosphenytoin** causes hypotension and is given with monitoring. Sodium valproate precipitates fatal hepatic failure in POLG mutations, while rapid fosphenytoin infusions induce cardiac arrhythmias.
